q: I swear by the Day of Qiyaamah!
v.s: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
v.c: I do swear by the Day of Judgment!

q: And I swear by the rebuking Nafs
(the inner voice that reprimands a person when he does wrong or when his good deeds are deficient)!
v.s: And I swear by the reproaching soul [to the certainty of resurrection].
v.c: And I do swear by the self-reproaching soul!

q: Does man think that We shall never gather his bones
(to resurrect him on the Day of Qiyaamah)?
v.s: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
v.c: Do people think We cannot reassemble their bones?

q: We have the power to perfect even his fingertips!
(When We resurrect him, We will even reproduce to perfection details as fine as his fingertips.)
v.s: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.
v.c: Yes ˹indeed˺! We are ˹most˺ capable of restoring ˹even˺ their very fingertips.

q: (He knows that if he believes in Qiyaamah, he will have to stop sinning in preparation for it.)
v.s: But man desires to continue in sin.
v.c: Still people want to deny what is yet to come,

q: asks, “When will the Day of Qiyaamah come?”
v.s: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
v.c: asking ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”

v.s: So when vision is dazzled.
v.c: But when the sight is stunned,

v.s: And the moon darkens.
v.c: and the moon is dimmed,

q: ...and the sun and moon will be joined
v.s: And the sun and the moon are joined,
v.c: and the sun and the moon are brought together,

q: ...man will say on that day, “Where is an escape?”
v.s: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the [place of] escape?"
v.c: on that Day one will cry, “Where is the escape?”

q: No! There is definitely no place of safety
v.s: No! There is no refuge.
v.c: But no! There will be no refuge.

q: On this day, the only abode
v.s: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
v.c: On that Day all will end up before your Lord.

q: On that day man will be informed of whatever
v.s: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back.
v.c: All will then be informed of what they have sent forth and left behind.

q: In reality, man will be well aware of himself
v.s: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,
v.c: In fact, people will testify against their own souls,

q: (in an attempt to prove his innocence).
v.s: Even if he presents his excuses.
v.c: despite the excuses they come up with.

q: (When revelation used to come to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he repented the words immediately upon hearing them, fearing that he would forget them. In this manner, the physical strain on him was increased. Affectionately advising him not to exert himself so much, Allaah says,)
Do not move your tongue with the
(Allaah commanded Rasulullaah ﷺ to first listen attentively to the recitation of the Qur'aan and only then to repeat the words.)
v.s: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muhammad], to hasten with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān].
v.c: Do not rush your tongue trying to memorize ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran.
v.h: The Prophet’s Rush to Memorize the Quran

q: Verily, it is Our responsibility to collect it
(to make you memorise the words of the Qur'aan)
and to make you recite it.
v.s: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.
v.c: It is certainly upon Us to ˹make you˺ memorize and recite it.

q: So when We have recited it
v.s: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.
v.c: So once We have recited a revelation ˹through Gabriel˺, follow its recitation ˹closely˺.

q: it is Our responsibility to make it clear.
(We will ensure that you are able to recite it clearly to people and to convey it to them.)
v.s: Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].
v.c: Then it is surely upon Us to make it clear ˹to you˺.

q: (Addressing those who deny the coming of Qiyaamah, Allaah says,)
(as you say. Qiyaamah will certainly take place).
v.s: No! But you [i.e., mankind] love the immediate
v.c: But no! In fact, you love this fleeting world,

v.s: And leave [i.e., neglect] the Hereafter.
v.c: and neglect the Hereafter.

v.s: [Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant,
v.c: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright,

v.s: Looking at their Lord.
v.c: looking at their Lord.

q: And many faces on that day will be gloomy...
v.s: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,
v.c: And ˹other˺ faces will be gloomy,

q: ...sensing that they will be dealt with most severely.
v.s: Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.
v.c: anticipating something devastating to befall them.

q: (This world can never be preferred over the Aakhirah, especially because people have to leave the world and everything in it behind when they die. Death is that time)
When the soul reaches the collar-bone...
v.s: No! When it [i.e., the soul] has reached the collar bones
v.c: But no! ˹Beware of the day˺ when the soul reaches the collar bone ˹as it leaves˺,

v.s: And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"
v.c: and it will be said, “Is there any healer ˹who can save this life˺?”

q: while certain that this is really the parting
(from this world and that none can save him).
v.s: And he [i.e., the dying one] is certain that it is the [time of] separation
v.c: And the dying person realizes it is ˹their˺ time to depart,

q: When one leg is planted close to the other
(as the dying person prepares for death)...
v.s: And the leg is wound about the leg,
v.c: and ˹then˺ their feet are tied together ˹in a shroud˺.

q: ...on this day you will be drawn towards your Rabb.
v.s: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.
v.c: On that day they will be driven to your Lord ˹alone˺.

q: (if the dying person was a Kaafir, his plight will be a terrible one because)
v.s: And he [i.e., the disbeliever] had not believed, nor had he prayed.
v.c: This denier neither believed nor prayed,

q: (from the one calling him to Islaam).
v.s: But [instead], he denied and turned away.
v.c: but persisted in denial and turned away,

q: (without regret and without searching for the truth)
he went to his family in arrogance
v.s: And then he went to his people, swaggering [in pride].
v.c: then went to their own people, walking boastfully.

v.s: Woe to you, and woe!
v.c: Woe to you, and more woe!

q: Woe to you yet again and again!
v.s: Then woe to you, and woe!
v.c: Again, woe to you, and even more woe!

q: Does man think that he will be left to be
(free without being required to fulfil Allaah's commands and without being called to account for his actions)?
v.s: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
v.c: Do people think they will be left without purpose?
v.h: Allah’s Ability to Create and Resurrect

v.s: Had he not been a sperm from semen emitted?
v.c: Were they not ˹once˺ a sperm-drop emitted?

q: ...after which he developed into a clot of blood and then He
v.s: Then he was a clinging clot, and [God] created [his form] and proportioned [him]
v.c: Then they became a clinging clot ˹of blood˺, then He developed and perfected their form,

v.s: And made of him two mates, the male and the female.
v.c: producing from it both sexes, male and female.

q: then not have the power to resurrect the dead
v.s: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?
v.c: Is such ˹a Creator˺ unable to bring the dead back to life?
